There's one aspect to it that I like to mention, just because it amuses me - the decline of traditional religion. Specifically, for many, their SJWdom fills the same space in their lives that past generations filled with religion.

Humans look for meaning in their lives. They look for a group to join, which group they expect to provide them with an identity. For many, the identity they're searching for is a moral one - they want to be seen to be fundamentally moral people, so they find and join an group that provides them with that identity. The most common traditional source of that was organized religion, but as organized religion has lost its appeal, new generations have had to look elsewhere. One of the most common places they've ended up is the SJW movement.

It provides pretty much all of the same benefits. They're a part of a defined group, with a designated set of fellow believers AND a ready-made set of evil enemies. They have a rigid and codified set of beliefs, and merely by demonstrating adherence to those beliefs, they signal to all the other true believers that they are of them, and therefore they are moral people. And they're protected from any need to actually consider those beliefs, since any and all who hold any different beliefs are evil heretics, and their opinions cannot matter. And on a regular basis, they can get together with all of their fellow believers and reaffirm their faith, and thus their sense of moral superiority.

Now - all that said, there's an uncomfortable additional bit - SJWs are by no means the only ones who do that sort of thing, and for the same basic reasons. In fact, that part of what drives pretty much anyone and everyone who adopts a label and its accompanying set of beliefs.
